subject.title: feat: add disableBoundaryAwareCache compat option for prefix-matching prompt cache providers

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose and auto-enable `compat.disableBoundaryAwareCache` for DeepSeek, or require a config-free internal provider capability instead?
rationale: The patch is technically credible, but automated review cannot decide whether a negative public compatibility knob and its DeepSeek upgrade default are the intended long-term product and API contract.

options.title: Adopt the compat contract
options.body: Accept the DeepSeek-only default with explicit `false` opt-out and merge the current sanitized, live-proven approach after final rebase review.

options.title: Internalize provider capability
options.body: Request the same DeepSeek message shaping behind an internal capability or default without exposing a new user-configurable field.

options.title: Select the config-free sibling
options.body: Pause this PR until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94945 or another replacement covers the production transport and supplies equally strong live proof.

recommendation.title: Adopt the compat contract
recommendation.body: Accept the DeepSeek-only default with explicit `false` opt-out and merge the current sanitized, live-proven approach after final rebase review.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history covers the provider cache-boundary behavior, exported compatibility types, and DeepSeek-adjacent defaults involved in this contract decision.
